questions.question_text:
If ‘→’ denotes increasing order of intensity, then the meaning of the words
[walk → jog → sprint] is analogous to [bothered → ________ → daunted].
Which one of the given options is appropriate to fill the blank?
questions.subtopic: Vocabulary: words, idioms, and phrases in context
questions.explaination: 'Walk -> jog -> sprint' depicts an increasing scale of physical speed/exertion. Similarly, 'bothered -> fazed -> daunted' depicts an increasing degree of perturbation/discouragement. 'Fazed' means disconcerted or perturbed, fitting between bothered and daunted.
questions.question_text_latex:
If `$\to$' denotes increasing order of intensity, then the meaning of the words $[\text{walk} \to \text{jog} \to \text{sprint}]$ is analogous to $[\text{bothered} \to \text{\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_} \to \text{daunted}]$.
Which one of the given options is appropriate to fill the blank?

questions.question_text:
Two wizards try to create a spell using all the four elements, water, air, fire, and
earth. For this, they decide to mix all these elements in all possible orders. They
also decide to work independently. After trying all possible combination of
elements, they conclude that the spell does not work.
How many attempts does each wizard make before coming to this conclusion,
independently?
questions.subtopic: Numerical computation and estimation: ratios, percentages, powers, exponents and logarithms, permutations and combinations, series
questions.explaination: There are 4 distinct elements (water, air, fire, earth). The number of distinct permutations/orderings of these 4 elements is $4! = 4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1 = 24$. Since each wizard tries all possible orders independently, each wizard makes 24 attempts.

questions.question_text:
In an engineering college of 10,000 students, 1,500 like neither their core branches
nor other branches. The number of students who like their core branches is 1/4th of
the number of students who like other branches. The number of students who like
both their core and other branches is 500.
The number of students who like their core branches is
questions.subtopic: Data interpretation: data graphs (bar graphs, pie charts, and other graphs representing data), 2- and 3-dimensional plots, maps, and tables
questions.explaination: Let $C$ and $O$ be sets of students liking core and other branches. Total students $N = 10000$, neither $= 1500$, so $|C \cup O| = 10000 - 1500 = 8500$. We are given $|C \cap O| = 500$ and $|C| = \frac{1}{4}|O| \implies |O| = 4|C|$. By inclusion-exclusion, $|C \cup O| = |C| + |O| - |C \cap O| \implies 8500 = |C| + 4|C| - 500 \implies 5|C| = 9000 \implies |C| = 1800$.

questions.explaination: From $\ln\left(\frac{x+y}{2}\right) = \frac{1}{2}[\ln(x) + \ln(y)] = \ln(\sqrt{xy})$, we obtain $\frac{x+y}{2} = \sqrt{xy} \implies x + y = 2\sqrt{xy} \implies (\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{y})^2 = 0 \implies x = y$. Substituting $x = y$ gives $\frac{x}{y} + \frac{y}{x} = 1 + 1 = 2$.

questions.question_text: In the sequence 6, 9, 14, x, 30, 41, a possible value of 𝑥 is
questions.subtopic: Numerical computation and estimation: ratios, percentages, powers, exponents and logarithms, permutations and combinations, series
questions.explaination: Examine the consecutive differences: $9 - 6 = 3$, $14 - 9 = 5$, $x - 14 = d_3$, $30 - x = d_4$, $41 - 30 = 11$. The differences are consecutive odd numbers: $3, 5, 7, 9, 11$. For $d_3 = 7$, $x = 14 + 7 = 21$, and checking $d_4 = 30 - 21 = 9$ matches. Hence, $x = 21$.
